dedupe_keys.name: imn costa rica climatological atlas and automatic weather station network

description: The National Meteorological Institute of Costa Rica (IMN) publishes a climatological atlas and live readings from its automatic weather stations. The atlas maps total monthly and annual rainfall, mean, maximum and minimum annual temperatures and sunshine hours, built from the stations of the IMN network for 1961 to 1980; the maps are digitised in GIS format and shown as high-resolution images at a scale of 1:1,600,000, with an interactive atlas, a manual and a product download, and the IMN presents it as an input for productivity, adaptation and climate resilience. The automatic stations page lists stations by region (North, Central and South Pacific, North Zone, Central Valley, North and South Caribbean), with their canton and province, status and a link to each station's data, including stations at airports, community water associations (ASADAs), farms and universities, and webcams. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the pages read, and the stations page warns that data may be delayed or stop and that the IMN takes no responsibility for it. Caveats: the atlas uses an old baseline period, and the pages are in Spanish. Coverage is Costa Rica. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation analysis of rainfall, heat and drought for water, energy and transport infrastructure; related records are the ANAM Burkina Faso climate services and the NEA Singapore real-time weather readings.
